Long conversational agents have become essen-
tial in our daily lives. They must remember
what was said long back in order to help us
efficiently complete a task without needing the
user to repeat instructions and context repeat-
edly. However, the main issue is that instruc-
tions and context change over time and so the
agents must be able to adapt accordingly. A
useful memory system should preserve both
current and historical states, distinguish stale
information from active knowledge, retrieve
evidence appropriate to the query and avoid
repeatedly invoking a large language model
to rewrite prior interactions. We introduce
MINDSET, a memory controller that stores
a conversation as immutable episodes and or-
ganizes them into versioned schemas through
minimum-energy state transitions. Each incom-
ing episode may reinforce, supersede, split or
create a schema. The transition decision

Let a conversation produce an ordered stream of
episodes
Et = (e1,e 2,...,e t),
where each episode stores a conversation identifier,
session, timestamp, speaker, raw text and locally
extracted entity, role, context, attribute, and change-
cue features. The memory controller maintains a
set of schemasSt. A schema groups compatible
episodes into a versioned state; it records support
and exception identifiers, a centroid and medoid,
validity bounds, active or historical status and pre-
decessor/successor links.
For each incoming episode et, the controller
chooses an action
at∈{REINFORCE,SUPERSEDE,SPLIT,NEW}
Reinforceadds evidence to a compatible active
schema.Supersedecloses an active schema and
creates its temporally linked successor.Splitcre-
ates a coexisting contextual branch.Newstarts an
independent schema. Raw episodes are immutable
under every action.

summarizing away evidence
At query time, a local router labels the information
need as current, historical, contextual or generic.
Three candidate channels are then combined:
• direct retrieval, a dense-BM25 union over raw
episodes;
• schema-mediated retrieval, which finds rele-
vant schemas and expands them back to their sup-
port, exception, medoid and continuity episodes;
• version retrieval, which exposes medoids from
active and historical schema states.
The candidate pool is reranked with
ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 and embeddings use
all-MiniLM-L6-v2. We use a candidate pool of
40 and return eight pieces of evidence. The answer
model receives the original provenance-bearing
episodes.

evidence.excerpt:
Retrieval methods can emit memory units of very
different size. We therefore normalize them be-
fore generation. Up to 20 candidate memories are
segmented into 768-token passages with 96-token
overlap, rescored against the question using the
same local embedding model and greedily selected
under a maximum of eight passages - 8,000 evi-
dence tokens and three passages per original mem-
ory. Every passage retains its source memory ID,
source event IDs, passage index, and character/-
token offsets. Long Context is the sole structural
exception because full history defines the baseline;
it uses deterministic recency truncation at 20,000
UTF-8 bytes.

evidence.excerpt:
We use a frozen manifest of 700 questions fromLo-
CoMo(Maharana et al., 2024), 70 from each of ten
conversations. The category counts are 151 single-
hop, 151 temporal, 96 multi-hop, 151 open-domain,
and 151 adversarial questions. As a secondary
dataset, we useMemoryAgentBench (MAB)(Hu
et al., 2026). We use 150 samples from benchmark-
instance files: 125 in-context-learning examples
and 25 recommendation examples. The five ICL
source groups contribute 25 instances each, and the
recommender contributes 25. We therefore use 850
questions in total. This is done intentionally to keep
API costs manageable while also providing suffi-
cient breadth for fair evaluation. The exact IDs and
order are stored in the manifest and will be released
with the codebase for reproducibility. Model trans-
fer is evaluated on the complete frozen LoCoMo
benchmark used by the primary experiment.

evidence.excerpt:
We compare MINDSET against 5 methods:
• Vector RAG:flat normalized MiniLM embed-
dings over timestamped dialogue turns with co-
sine top-kretrieval.
• Long Context Memory:chronological full his-
tory, with deterministic oldest-turn removal only
beyond 20,000 UTF-8 bytes.
• MemoryBank:adapted from the official archi-
tecture (Zhong et al., 2023). GPT-OSS replaces
the original GPT-3.5 summarizer so the backbone
remains same.
• LightMem:a reproduction preserving key de-
sign choices from the paper (Zhang et al., 2026).
• Nemori:a reproduction of the official implemen-
tation (Ma et al., 2026).

evidence.excerpt:
The primary model is gpt-oss-120b from Cere-
bras. All six methods use the same answer instruc-
tions, deterministic temperature 0, a maximum out-
put reservation of 4,096 tokens, structured JSON
validation, and completeness retries. Primary Lo-
CoMo batching uses eight questions where sup-
ported; Long Context uses one question per request
because histories are question-specific and large.
The cross-backbone experiment uses zai-glm-4.7
and gemma-4-31b from Cerebras, 1 question per re-
quest, a 1,024-token output cap and a 160,000-byte

remains directionally positive

Replacing energy-based assignment with nearest-
schema merging and removing fragmentation pres-
sure drop F1 by 0.0200 and 0.0237 respectively,
showing the most impact. They support the cen-
tral proposal: it matters not only whether rele-
vant episodes can be found, but whether memory
evolves into a useful number of coherent states.
The other terms show smaller individual effects.
Their retrieval columns except provenance expan-
sion almost tie the full system as they affect how
evidence is organized more than the presence of
candidate episodes.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final evaluation uses standard benchmark ground truth and deterministic matching, fully separate from the heuristic development calibration.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic rule-based NLP metrics (token F1, exact match, Recall@k, MRR, nDCG) computed against benchmark ground truth on frozen manifests, with no LLM judge used for any reported number.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Hand-tuned compatibility coefficients, energy weights, transition thresholds, and hysteresis margins calibrated on a disjoint 300-question LoCoMo development set, with no gradient fitting or test-answer F1 optimization.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are carefully calibrated with empirical results, distinguishing between statistically confirmed improvements in retrieval metrics and directional but unconfirmed gains in answer generation.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted across 850 questions spanning LoCoMo and MemoryAgentBench against 5 baseline memory architectures, incorporating ablation variants and cross-backbone testing with GLM-4.7 and Gemma-4-31B. It employs cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm-corrected permutation tests, explicitly acknowledging where differences (such as answer F1 against LightMem) are not statistically significant.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The test evaluation relies entirely on standard benchmark ground truth and deterministic rule-based matching, remaining fully independent of the heuristic development calibration.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic standard NLP metrics (token F1, exact match, Recall@k, MRR, nDCG) evaluated on frozen benchmark manifests across multiple frozen LLM backbones with no LLM judges.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Hand-tuned engineering heuristics and threshold calibration conducted on a disjoint 300-question LoCoMo development set, with no model gradient updates or answer-F1 optimization.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently document limitations, including heuristic tuning of transition weights on a development set, lower absolute performance on MemoryAgentBench, and baseline substitutions where official artifacts were unavailable.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is comprehensively detailed, specifying formal definitions and exact parameters for transition signals, compatibility scoring, energy terms, hysteresis boundaries, and evidence retrieval adapters without learned end-to-end parameters or test-set optimization.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a methodologically rigorous, thoroughly tested memory architecture with controlled comparative experiments, rigorous statistical reporting, and well-substantiated, unexaggerated claims.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces MINDSET, an energy-based memory controller for conversational agents that organizes immutable dialogue episodes into versioned schemas via discrete state-transition actions (reinforce, supersede, split, new) under an explicit energy formulation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a methodologically rigorous, thoroughly tested memory architecture with controlled comparative experiments, rigorous statistical reporting, and well-substantiated, unexaggerated claims.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently document limitations, including heuristic tuning of transition weights on a development set, lower absolute performance on MemoryAgentBench, and baseline substitutions where official artifacts were unavailable.
